case_title: KULWANT SINGH & ORS. v. STATE OF PUNJAB
aggravating_circumstances: Dowry death, Harassment for dowry, Poisoning
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to 7 years RI and 1 year RI under s.498A, fine of Rs.500/-
neutral_facts: The accused, a married man and his in-laws, were involved in the death of a married woman under suspicious circumstances. The deceased died due to aluminium phosphide poisoning within seven years of her marriage. She was subjected to harassment for dowry by the accused and his in-laws. The harassment continued until almost immediately before her death. The post-mortem examination revealed the presence of aluminium phosphide in her body, indicating poisoning. The FIR was lodged after the chemical examination report was received, and the investigation led to the filing of charges against the accused. The trial court convicted the accused under Sections 304-B and 498-A of the IPC, and the High Court upheld the conviction. The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, affirming the conviction and sentence.
